challenge.reason: The old ADR forbids writing secrets anywhere under .faff/, not only committing them. Caching resolved API keys in .faff/cache/credentials.json writes plaintext secrets to disk, which is the exact thing the ADR rules out; gitignore only prevents commits, not exposure through backups, cage mounts, log or artifact uploads. The why never engages the old rationale, and the claimed gain (avoiding a process.env read, which is an in-memory lookup) is negligible and could be had with an in-process cache without touching disk. The supersession argument is unsound.
